promptLatex: How many ways are there to distribute 12 identical candies to 4 distinct children if each child must receive at least 2 candies?
hintLatex:
Give 2 candies to each child first, using 8 candies. Then distribute the remaining 4 candies freely among the 4 children.
The number of ways is \binom{4+4-1}{4-1} = \binom{7}{3}.
solutionLatex:
Give 2 candies to each of the 4 children, using 8 candies total. Then distribute the remaining 4 candies freely among the 4 children (nonnegative solutions).

Number of ways: \binom{4+4-1}{4-1} = \binom{7}{3} = 35.
